newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks seen up slightly on IMF news.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks seen up slightly on IMF news.

text.p: Thai stocks, which gained in the last four trading days, were expected to rise slightly on Wednesday as investors waited to see what sort of advice or aid Thailand will take from the IMF, brokers said.

"I think investors will continue to buy but on a selective basis today. The market has risen quite high and investors are expected to buy more carefully as they don't want to take risks. The only positive factor seen now is the IMF news," said Payuha Boonsiri of Nithipat Capital.
The composite SET index closed 1.49 points higher to 682.16 on Tuesday. The SET-50 index rose 0.16 point to 52.17.
Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya has said he would meet five officials of IMF this week in Bangkok to seek their advice on ways to revive the country's battered economy.
Brokers said another factor which was could slow down buying was anticipation ahead of the release of the country's key economic indicators by the central bank which is scheduled for Thursday.
